features: TOUCHES THE DATABASE: THREE NEW COLUMNS ON THE ACCOUNTING ENTRIES, NO DATA REWRITTEN — A new migration, which the update runs by itself, adds three columns to the table scritture_contabili: imputazione and imputazione_nota, where the program writes what a payment went to and the note left by whoever recorded it, and natura_storno, where it writes why a payment was reversed. It rewrites no data: the payments and reversals recorded before have the three columns empty, the payment page says so («Non dichiarata: registrato prima che il programma la chiedesse», not declared: recorded before the program asked for it; «Natura non dichiarata: stornato prima che il programma la chiedesse», nature not declared: reversed before the program asked for it) and no recorded amount changes. Two figures that the program calculates do change, though: the overdue amount on the instalment plan page, which no longer counts instalments not yet issued or the one that falls due today, and the money expected in the cash forecast (point (a), below). Each of the three columns has its own check: a run interrupted halfway resumes from where it had got to, and where it has already run it does nothing. No new permission, no new library, the requirements do not change. Two things to know after the update. (a) The colour of the traffic light of the cash forecast («Tesoreria a 30gg», 30-day treasury) can change where an instalment mixes one person's debt and another person's credit, typically instalment 0 of the carried-over balance: before, one person's credit took expected money off the other's debt, now it does not (in a test case the light goes from red to yellow). (b) Reload the pages that are already open: the payment form now makes a new request to the program.

CHANGES: REVERSING A PAYMENT ASKS WHY, AND THE DATE DEPENDS ON THE ANSWER — Before, the correcting entry of a reversal always had the date of the reversal, in the server's day. Now the confirmation for reversing a payment, from the menu of the list, asks «Perché lo storni?» (why are you reversing it?) with two answers, neither already chosen, and without an answer it cannot be confirmed: «Registrazione sbagliata: il versamento non c'è mai stato, o va registrato di nuovo in un altro modo. Lo storno vale dal giorno del versamento.» (wrong entry: the payment never happened, or has to be recorded again in another way; the reversal applies from the day of the payment) and «Il versamento c'era ed è tornato indietro (assegno insoluto, addebito respinto, bonifico richiamato). Lo storno vale da oggi.» (the payment was there and came back: bounced cheque, rejected debit, recalled transfer; the reversal applies from today). Next to each answer the confirmation writes from which date it applies; if it cannot find out, it says so. With the first, the correcting entry, the compensations and the shares take the date of the payment (each the date of the entry it reverses): on the days between the payment and the reversal it is as if the payment had never happened, both in the cash and in the person's debt. If the financial year that contains the date of the payment is closed, or does not exist, the reversal applies from today and the confirmation says so first. With the second, the correcting entry and the shares take today's date: the money was there, and until today it shows as collected. If the payment was made only with credit, without money, the two answers speak of the compensation: «La compensazione è sbagliata: si toglie dal giorno in cui è stata fatta.» (the compensation is wrong: it is removed from the day it was made) and «La compensazione era giusta e si annulla da oggi.» (the compensation was right and is cancelled from today). The answer is written on the reversed payment and is not remembered for the next reversal. Reversing a credit refund, which starts from the account statement, asks nothing and works as before. «Today» is the administrator's day (the Rome time zone), not the server's.

CHANGES: THE PAYMENT FORM ASKS «CHI HA SCELTO A CHE COSA VA?» WHEN THE PAYMENT DOES NOT FOLLOW THE ORDER OF DUE DATES — The automatic split goes by due date, oldest first, issued or not; with the same due date, first the carried-over balance (instalment 0), then the issued instalments, then those not yet issued. It is the order the program proposes, and the program works it out with a single rule: the browser no longer rewrites it. Before saving, the form asks the program whether the split follows it. If an older instalment stays open, even of another unit or another management of the same person, above «Conferma incasso» (confirm payment) it says which one (the due date, whether it is not yet issued, the unit, the management and how much is left) and asks «Chi ha scelto a che cosa va?» (who chose what it goes to?), with two answers and none already chosen: «Indicata da chi ha versato» (indicated by whoever paid: the description of the bank transfer, a phone call) and «Scelta da te» (chosen by you). The note is optional for both. The one for «Indicata da chi ha versato» is printed on the receipt, so write the words of whoever paid; the one for «Scelta da te» stays on the payment page and does not go on the receipt: the field says so, and changing the choice empties the note. If you arrive from a payment reported through the portal, «Indicata da chi ha versato» is already chosen as long as the payment goes to the reported instalment. In the form, «Conferma incasso» turns on once you have chosen. The program, however, does not refuse the payment: if the choice does not arrive (the order check did not succeed, or the request does not come from this form) it marks it «Fuori ordine, non dichiarata» (out of order, not declared). If it cannot check the order it says so, shows the choice anyway, optional, and the payment goes through. A payment made only with credit is marked «Compensazione con il credito» (compensation with the credit). The question appears when the split departs from the order (or when it could not be checked): if the payment follows it, not one more click. An approved instalment that is not yet issued, with its due date passed, counts too: every payment that leaves it open and puts money on later instalments departs from the order, until the instalment is paid. The payment guide has a new section, «Quando il versamento non segue l'ordine delle scadenze».

CHANGES: IN THE PAYMENT FORM THE «SCADUTA» BADGE APPEARS, AND «MOSTRA SCADUTE» AND «PAGA SCADUTE» READ THE DUE DATE — The «Scaduta» (overdue) badge never appeared. Now it appears on issued instalments whose due date has passed and which have a balance; an instalment not yet issued with a past date says «No emissione» (not issued), as before. «Mostra scadute» (show overdue) and «Paga scadute» (pay overdue) take the instalments whose due date has passed, including those not yet issued (their title says so), and the day of the due date is not yet overdue. «Mostra scadute» no longer keeps the carried-over rows that are not yet due: before, it always kept those with «saldo», «rata 0» or «pregresso» in the description too. The «Debito pregresso» (carried-over debt) and «Credito pregresso» (carried-over credit) are recognised from instalment 0, not from the words of the description.

CHANGES: THE INSTALMENT PLAN PAGE SAYS «SCADUTO DA INCASSARE», AND «PAGATO IL» SAYS THE RIGHT PAYMENT — The «Da Incassare» card is called «Scaduto da incassare» (overdue to collect) and the «Scadute» column «Scaduto»: they count the issued instalments that are overdue, from the day after the due date, in the administrator's day, and no longer drafts or the instalment that falls due today. Before, the page compared dates in the browser with the browser's clock and also counted the day itself and the instalments not yet issued: in a test case the same person had € 100.00 overdue on one page and € 300.00 on another. The tooltip of the card says: «Le rate emesse con la scadenza passata, meno quanto già versato: anche il pregresso della rata 0, se è emessa.» (the issued instalments with a past due date, minus what has already been paid: also the carried-over balance of instalment 0, if it is issued) and, below it: «Una rata è scaduta dal giorno dopo la sua scadenza. Le rate non ancora emesse restano fuori. Non sottrae i crediti di altre rate; dentro una rata, sì.» (an instalment is overdue from the day after its due date; instalments not yet issued stay out; it does not subtract the credits of other instalments; within an instalment, it does). «Pagato il» (paid on) says the date of the last payment that was not reversed: before, after reversing a payment, it said the date of the reversal. The correcting entry of a reversal does not count as a payment, nor does the credit taken for another instalment.

CHANGES: THE CASH FORECAST SPLITS OVERDUE INSTALMENTS FROM THOSE FALLING DUE AND NAMES THE PEOPLE IN ARREARS — In the «Tesoreria a 30gg» of the dashboard «Rate in Arr.» becomes «Rate scadute» (overdue instalments) and «Rate in scadenza» (instalments falling due, within 30 days). The money expected from a person is their instalments to pay minus their credit in the same management, taken off the oldest instalment, never another person's credit; the subtitle of «Rate scadute» says «al netto del credito di ognuno nella stessa gestione» (net of each person's credit in the same management). Below, «Rate scadute dei condòmini» (overdue instalments of the owners) appears: the first five people by overdue amount, with the unit, «in ritardo di N giorni» (N days late, the oldest instalment), the link to their account statement and, if there is one, the credit written under the name. A person's overdue amount is gross: the credit is shown and not subtracted. «e altri N» (and N others) says how many more people are late, and the bands «1–30 giorni», «31–90 giorni» and «oltre 90 giorni» (1–30 days, 31–90 days, over 90 days) give the overdue amount of everyone. «Pregressi non pagati» is now called «Fatture pregresse non pagate» (unpaid earlier invoices): they are the debts to suppliers overdue from before. «Today» is the administrator's day also for the 30-day limit and for the starting day of the forecast. «Verifica o Sollecita Incassi» (check or chase payments) still leads to the list of payments: the program does not send reminders.

CHANGES: THE PORTAL SAYS «IN ATTESA DI EMISSIONE» FOR AN INSTALMENT NOT YET ISSUED — The reminder of an instalment is born when the plan is approved, before issue. Before, with the date passed, the portal wrote «Scaduta», and in the days before «Scade tra N gg» (due in N days) in red or yellow. Now, for an instalment not yet issued (not instalment 0, which stays «Debito Pregresso», carried-over debt), in the 14 days before the date and after it has passed, it writes «In attesa di emissione» (awaiting issue), in grey; beyond 14 days the usual wording stays. The owner's window does not put a red title on an instalment not yet issued. The administrator's reminder «Emettere rata N» does not change: with the date passed it stays red, with «Emetti subito» (issue now).

CHANGES: TODAY'S DATE IN THE FORMS IS THE DATE OF WHOEVER USES THEM — Before, the date proposed in the forms came from the day in Greenwich: between midnight and 1 a.m. in Rome (2 a.m. in summer) it was still yesterday, and on 1 January it was still the year before. Now it is the day of whoever uses the page. It applies to the date of a payment, the issue date of an instalment (which creates the amount due), a payment to a supplier, new and edited, the date of an invoice, the transfer between funds, the immediate settlement, the F24 form (the date of the payment, that of the reversal and «stampato il», printed on), the refund from the account statement, the agenda and the dashboard, the closed ownerships in the list of units and the balance sheet. The due date of an invoice, the document date plus the supplier's days, no longer loses a day when the sum crosses the change to summer time in March. The date filter of the agenda could start from the day before, and now it starts from the chosen day. In the program, «today» for a reversal is the administrator's day.

CHANGES: THE PAYMENT PAGE SAYS WHO RECORDED IT, WHAT IT GOES TO AND WHY IT WAS REVERSED — Before, the subtitle always said «Registrato da Sistema» (recorded by System) and the box of a reversed payment «Operatore: Sconosciuto» (operator: unknown), because the program did not write who recorded or who reversed, and the page looked for the reversal where it was not. Now the subtitle says «Registrato da …» when it knows, and the program writes who records and who reverses. There is the line «Imputazione» (allocation): «Secondo l'ordine delle scadenze» (following the order of due dates), «Indicata da chi ha versato», «Scelta dall'amministratore» (chosen by the administrator) (both with the note), «Fuori ordine, non dichiarata» or «Compensazione con il credito». A reversed payment has the box with «Stornato il» (reversed on), «Vale dal» (applies from), «Perché» (why) and «Stornato da» (reversed by). For a payment declared or marked out of order, not reversed, a sentence says how to correct it: «Se la dichiarazione non è giusta: nell'elenco degli incassi, dal menu della riga, «Storna» con «Registrazione sbagliata», poi registralo di nuovo con la data del versamento.» (if the declaration is not right: in the list of payments, from the row menu, «Storna» with «Registrazione sbagliata», then record it again with the date of the payment). A payment cannot be edited: it is reversed and recorded again.

NEW: THE RECEIPT PRINTS THE CRITERION OF THE ALLOCATION, AND THE LIST OF PAYMENTS HAS THE FILTER «FUORI ORDINE, NON DICHIARATA» — Above the table of the shares the receipt has a line: «Imputazione: secondo l'ordine delle scadenze.», «Imputazione: indicata da chi ha versato: «the note».» (the note is theirs, you write it in their words), «Imputazione: scelta dall'amministratore.» (without the note, which stays internal) or «Imputazione: compensazione con il credito.» (allocation: following the order of due dates; indicated by whoever paid; chosen by the administrator; compensation with the credit). For a payment «Fuori ordine, non dichiarata» and for earlier payments the line is not there. The receipt window shows the same line before printing; the text of the email does not carry it, the attached PDF does. In the list of payments the status filter has one more choice, «Fuori ordine, non dichiarata», to find again the payments on which nobody chose (cancelled ones are not counted).

CHANGES: THE RECEIPTS — THE MENU ON ONE LINE AND SIX CORRECTIONS — In the payment menu «Stampa o invia ricevuta» (print or send receipt) fits on one line. Then: (1) an outcome that arrives when the batch window was closed or reopened while the request was travelling goes in the line at the top of the page and, if the window is reopened, also in a line of the window, and if the request wrote something (print, archive, sending) the preview is redone: before, the outcome of an old request showed up in the new window, and with the window closed it showed up nowhere. (2) An expired session says «La sessione è scaduta: ricarica la pagina e, se serve, accedi di nuovo.» (the session has expired: reload the page and, if needed, sign in again) and no longer «Unauthenticated.». (3) If a web page or a file that is not a PDF arrives, the tab closes and a sentence says so; a real PDF with a generic file type opens. (4) A missing permission says «Non hai il permesso di fare questa operazione. Se ti serve, chiedilo a chi ti ha dato l'accesso.» (you do not have permission to do this; if you need to, ask whoever gave you access). (5) The preview with the tab closed by hand no longer downloads the file. (6) Reopening the address of a print goes back to the receipts page with the filters you had chosen, one per condominium; the default filters, which carry that day's dates, are not remembered, and opening the page without filters starts again from the default ones.

HOW IT WORKS TODAY, WHERE IT MAKES A DIFFERENCE — (1) The order of due dates is the program's proposal, not a rule of law: whoever paid may indicate something else, and the program records your choice. The program works out the allocation a moment before recording: if at the same instant someone else records a payment of the same person, the label may not reflect the latest one. It is a label, not a figure. (2) A person's overdue amount counts issued instalments: an instalment issued with a future issue date is «Scaduto da incassare» on the plan page and carries the «Scaduta» badge in the form, but does not enter the cash forecast until the date arrives. (3) The cash forecast reads the journal: it does not include the carried-over balance of the balances not yet in a plan, nor that of instalment 0 not yet issued. (4) «Today» is the Rome day for the program and the day of your browser for the proposed dates: for whoever has the browser in another time zone, for example in the United Kingdom, between 23:00 and 24:00 local time the proposed date may be the day before. (5) If printing a receipt fails after you have closed its window, in the list of payments and on the payment page the PDF tab closes without a sentence; on the receipts page the sentence is there, at the top of the page. (6) The PDF of a print does not reopen after you reload the receipts page: the browser frees the file; you save it from the viewer, or redo it from the page (it comes out as «Copia»). (7) With «Versato da» (paid by), the extra part goes to an instalment of whoever paid: it pays what is left to pay, and the rest becomes their credit; the sentence above the choice says so. (8) On the instalment plan page the «per unità» (by unit) tab and the «per persona» (by person) tab remove the credit within the same group (the people of a unit, the units of a person): the two tabs may give different figures for the same plan. (9) The order of due dates does not tell managements or funds apart: it proposes paying the oldest instalment of any management first, and it does not know that an instalment belongs to a restricted fund. If whoever paid meant a fund or a special-works instalment, you choose the rows and answer the question.
